title: Text Preprocessing Quiz
description: Test your understanding of text preprocessing

questions.question: What is tokenization in Natural Language Processing?
options: The process of encrypting text data
The process of breaking text into smaller units like words or sentences
The process of translating text to another language
The process of removing all punctuation from text
questions.explanation: Tokenization is the process of breaking text into smaller units called tokens, which can be words, sentences, characters, or subwords. This is a fundamental preprocessing step in NLP.

questions.question: Which tokenization strategy would be most appropriate for a character-level language model?
options: Word tokenization
Sentence tokenization
Character tokenization
Paragraph tokenization
questions.explanation: Character tokenization breaks text into individual characters, which is ideal for character-level language models that learn patterns at the character level rather than word level.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of converting text to lowercase during preprocessing?
options: It makes the text easier to read
It reduces vocabulary size by treating 'The' and 'the' as the same word
It improves the visual appearance of the text
It removes all punctuation automatically
questions.explanation: Lowercasing reduces vocabulary size by treating words with different capitalizations as the same token (e.g., 'The' and 'the'), which helps models generalize better and reduces memory requirements.

questions.question: What are stopwords in NLP?
options: Words that stop the tokenization process
Common words like 'the', 'is', 'and' that carry little semantic meaning
Words that contain punctuation marks
Words that appear only once in a document
questions.explanation: Stopwords are common words (like 'the', 'is', 'and', 'or') that appear frequently but typically carry little semantic meaning. They are often removed to reduce noise and focus on content words.

questions.question: What is stemming in text preprocessing?
options: Removing the first letter of each word
Reducing words to their root form by removing suffixes (e.g., 'running' → 'run')
Capitalizing the first letter of each word
Splitting compound words into separate tokens
questions.explanation: Stemming reduces words to their root form by removing suffixes. For example, 'running', 'runs', and 'ran' might all be reduced to 'run'. This helps group related words together and reduces vocabulary size.

questions.question: When should you keep punctuation during text preprocessing?
options: Never, punctuation should always be removed
Always, punctuation is always important
When it carries semantic meaning, such as in sentiment analysis where '!' and '?' matter
Only when the text is in English
questions.explanation: Punctuation should be kept when it carries semantic meaning. For example, in sentiment analysis, '!' and '?' can indicate strong emotions or questions. However, for tasks like topic modeling, punctuation may be less important.

questions.question: What is a vocabulary in the context of text preprocessing?
options: A dictionary for looking up word definitions
The set of unique tokens found in the text corpus
A list of all stopwords
The original text before preprocessing
questions.explanation: A vocabulary is the set of unique tokens (words, characters, or subwords) found in a text corpus after tokenization. It represents all the distinct units that the model will work with.

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of aggressive stemming?
options: It increases vocabulary size
It makes processing slower
It may produce non-words and lose semantic distinctions (e.g., 'university' → 'univers')
It requires more memory
questions.explanation: Aggressive stemming can produce non-words (like 'univers' from 'university') and may conflate words with different meanings. This can lead to loss of semantic information and reduced model performance.

questions.question: Why is consistent preprocessing important across training and test data?
options: To make the code run faster
To prevent distribution mismatch and ensure the model sees data in the same format
To reduce the file size of the dataset
To make the text more readable
questions.explanation: Consistent preprocessing ensures that training and test data have the same format and distribution. Inconsistent preprocessing can lead to distribution mismatch, poor model performance, and unexpected errors.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of character tokenization over word tokenization?
options: It produces shorter sequences
It's faster to compute
It has no out-of-vocabulary issues and works for any language
It preserves more semantic meaning
questions.explanation: Character tokenization has no out-of-vocabulary (OOV) issues because any word can be represented as a sequence of characters. It also works universally across languages without needing language-specific rules.
